text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm proposing we reorg the console telemetry + the placement of role checks to reduce dashboard fanout and improve tenant SLOs. Short version: run a cheap ingress access-filter to compute allowed scopes, cache that per-request, and avoid per-panel auth queries that blow up QPS. Thoughts?

kevin: Can you sketch where the current hot path is? I know we've seen spikes during heavy dashboards but want the exact hotspots.

maria: Current pattern: panels expand into many sub-queries (time/series slices) and each sub-query does an authorization call against the access service. So a single dashboard can produce hundreds of auth checks and queries.

lee: This matches what I saw in the trace samples. Most of the auth calls are identical (same user + tenant subset) but we aren't deduping. That plus lack of caching = tail latencies.

sam: Is the idea to move auth earlier in the pipeline and compute "allowed_scopes" once per request and then filter panels by that set?

maria: Exactly. Pseudocode:```# ingress
allowed = access_service.get_allowed_scopes(user)
for panel in dashboard: if panel.scope in allowed: run_query(panel)
else: render_empty(panel)
```This avoids the N auth calls and lets us cache allowed per-request or short TTL.

kevin: Tradeoffs? I'm thinking about permission changes and stale caches. If we cache too long we might leak access.

lee: We can keep TTL short (e.g., 30s) and still get most dedupe wins. For permission changes we support explicit invalidation hooks (KMS events / admin API) for immediate revocation. Still, there is a window — but it's similar to other caches we use.

sam: Another concern: some panels are generated server-side with dynamic filter expansion (e.g., derived queries that compute per-tenant sub-aggregation). Pre-filtering may not be enough if the panel expansion depends on result contents.

maria: Good point. For panels that expand based on data, we need a hybrid: run a compact pre-query that returns candidate keys, intersect with allowed_scopes, then expand only the allowed ones. That adds an extra lightweight query but reduces the number of heavyweight expansions.

kevin: Can we quantify expected savings? Even rough ballpark helps for prioritization.

lee: From load tests: for a 50-panel dashboard where auth is currently per-expanded-shard, we saw ~6x auth calls. If we dedupe + cache we drop total requests by ~70% and reduce P95 by ~30-40% in the heavy-case test.

maria: Metrics we should collect during rollout:
- auth_check_time_ms (per-request and p95/p99)
- dashboard_query_count_per_request
- allowed_scopes_cache_hit_rate
- panel_tail_latency_p95_p99
- failure_rate_on_prefilter_path

sam: Also track correctness: diff counts between current path and new path (how many panels get filtered out). We should run an A/B that compares output hashes for a sample of dashboards.

kevin: Implementation plan idea: 1) infra-only change — add ingress stage that queries access-service and returns allowed set (opt-in via header). 2) Console codepath opt-in flag to use prefilter. 3) Canary on 5% traffic, metric checks, 4) ramp + invalidate fallback.

lee: We need to be careful with RBAC semantics. Some permissions are resource-attribute based (e.g., "view if team==X") so the allowed set is not just tenant id list; it can be predicate expressions. We should represent allowed_scopes as typed predicates and provide client helpers to evaluate cheaply before expanding.

maria: Agreed. For MVP we can handle the common case (explicit tenant and workspace IDs). We'll return a schema that supports both explicit ids and simple predicates for advanced cases. The console will fall back to the old path if predicate type unknown.

opsbot: deploy-bot: note — there is a permissions-service release planned tomorrow that adds batch_allowed_scopes endpoint. Coordination required.

sam: Good — that batch endpoint is what ingress should call. Can we get latency guarantees? If batch_allowed_scopes is >50ms it could be a problem.

lee: We should also consider local LRU caching of allowed sets keyed by (user, role_version) to avoid calling the access service for frequent refreshes. We already maintain role_version in the token metadata.

kevin: Migration checks: smoke tests to assert that for the canary group DASH_OUTPUT_HASH_NEW == DASH_OUTPUT_HASH_OLD for 95% of dashboards (allow small diffs for time windows). Add an integrity alert if diffs > threshold.

maria: Owners: Maria (product) to own rollout plan + dashboards to monitor; Lee (eng) to prototype prefilter in console and helper libs; Sam (eng-platform) to add ingress call + cache & canary gating; Kevin (SRE) to own metrics/alerts. Timeline: prototype 2 weeks, canary 3rd week, ramp during 4th week if metrics look good.

lee: I'll start a small spike PR for the console helper and sample traces to show improvement.

sam: I'll wire the ingress call and a feature flag. We'll need a feature flag that can be toggled per-tenant for the canary.

kevin: I'll prep the dashboards and SLOs to watch. Add heatmap for per-tenant query count.

maria: Action items:
- lee: PR for console prefilter helper + tests (due in 10 days)
- sam: ingress batch_allowed_scopes call + per-tenant flag (due in 10 days)
- kevin: metrics dashboard + canary alert thresholds (due in 7 days)
- maria: open RFC issue with design + migration playbook (today)

lee: Quick note — for the SQL-backed panels we can push some predicate evaluation into the DB: e.g., add WHERE tenant_id IN (allowed) early in the plan so the DB prunes rows. That will also reduce network payload. Example SQL tweak:```SELECT ts, sum(val) FROM events WHERE tenant_id IN (:allowed) AND ts > :start GROUP BY ts;```

sam: Sounds good. Also add a small synthetic test that simulates permission churn to validate invalidation path.

maria: Thanks team. I'll open the RFC and tag owners. If no objections I'll schedule the spike kick-off tomorrow. :+1:

kevin: +1

lee: +1

sam: +1
